stories.title: Koeppel Rosen Arranges Three Office Leases in Midtown, Midtown South
stories.excerpt: Koeppel Rosen LLC, leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, has arranged nearly 18,000 square feet of new office space leases, comprised of separate transactions at three different properties in the company’s portfolio. Max Koeppel represented Koeppel Rosen in-house on all three leases. The transactions include the following: MNRK Music Group L.P., an independent music company, has agreed to a 7,629 rentable-square-foot lease across the entire ninth floor at 443 Park Avenue South. The lease includes a 7-year, 7-month term and the space will be used as an office for the tenant. Luke Dillmeier, Patrick Heeg, and Thomas Hines with Transwestern represented the tenant. AL Diamond Home Products LLC, an importer and distributor of household goods, has agreed to a 7,272 rentable-square-foot lease across the entire fifth floor at 20 West 36th Street. The lease includes a 7-year, 7-month term and the space will be used as an office for the tenant. Joel Kubie with Benchmark represented the tenant. Kevin V. Lehman DDS, a New York City dental practice, has agreed to a 3,096 rentable-square-foot lease on a partial fourth floor space at 154 West 14th Street. The lease includes a 12-year, 10-month term and the space will be used as a dentist’s office. Todd Hershmann and Josh Gosin with Newmark represented the tenant. The post Koeppel Rosen Arranges Three Office Leases in Midtown, Midtown South appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Koeppel Rosen arranged 18,000 SF office leases across three Midtown/Midtown South properties.
Portfolio-level leasing activity indicates modest tenant demand in prime NYC office.
No supply or demand signal material to multifamily development strategy.
stories.summary: Koeppel Rosen LLC closed approximately 18,000 square feet of new office leases across three separate properties in its Midtown and Midtown South portfolio. Max Koeppel represented the landlord on all transactions. The leases reflect continued albeit selective tenant activity in Manhattan's core office markets.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily. Office leasing momentum in Midtown does not meaningfully signal residential demand; Manhattan's bifurcated market means office weakness does not drive apartment construction or occupancy uplift.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 490-Unit Multifamily in St. Louis
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced the sale of Trinity Park Apartments, a 490-unit multifamily property in North St. Louis. The property was sold through an online live bid auction sale conducted by Marcus & Millichap. “Trinity Park Apartments offered investors a significant value-add opportunity,” said Ryan D. Engle, senior managing director investments. “The property’s below-market occupancy presented a substantial lease-up opportunity for the new ownership.” Engle, Andrean Angelov and Aaron Kuroiwa, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Chicago Oak Brook and Indianapolis offices, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller. Engle and Angelov, along with Mike Cusick in the firm’s St. Louis office, procured the buyer. The agents collaborated with Adam Sklaver and Philip Kates of Marcus & Millichap’s auction services to market the asset and assist in securing the buyer. Trinity Park Apartments, located at 11065 Dunklin Drive, spans 24.08 acres and consists of 34 residential buildings including 285 one-bedroom and 205 two-bedroom residences. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 490-Unit Multifamily in St. Louis appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold 490-unit Trinity Park Apartments, North St. Louis via auction.
Below-market occupancy presents value-add/lease-up opportunity for new owner.
Distressed asset movement signals soft demand conditions in North St. Louis submarket.
stories.summary: Trinity Park Apartments, a 490-unit multifamily property in North St. Louis, sold via online live bid auction facilitated by Marcus & Millichap. The property spans 24.08 acres with 285 one-bedroom and 205 two-bedroom units across 34 buildings. The sale highlighted below-market occupancy and substantial lease-up upside for the buyer.
stories.impact: North St. Louis multifamily faces absorption headwinds; below-market occupancy suggests oversupply relative to demand in the submarket. New development in this area should be carefully underwritten for tenant demand before capital commitment; pricing pressure and slower rent growth likely limit development IRRs.

stories.title: Hanover Company Launches Construction on Its First SoCal Industrial
stories.excerpt: Hanover Company, alongside its capital partner, a real estate fund advised by Crow Holdings Capital, has begun construction on a ground-up industrial development in Simi Valley. The project marks the developer’s debut in the region. The approximately 200,000-square-foot building sits on a 13-acre site at 903 Quimisa Drive. With immediate proximity to CA 118, the project will feature 36’ clear heights, an 8.5” slab, skylights and ample employee parking. “We are thrilled to bring Hanover Industrial’s first project to Southern California and to establish a presence in the dynamic Simi Valley market,” said Anthony Feenick, development partner at Hanover Company. “We are grateful for our continued partnership with the team at Crow Holdings Capital on this endeavor and look forward to seeing the project come to fruition.” Located off the 118 freeway, the project is designed to accommodate a variety of users, including corporate headquarters, packaging and assembly or distribution. The post Hanover Company Launches Construction on Its First SoCal Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hanover Company, Crow Holdings Capital begin 200K SF industrial project in Simi Valley, CA.
Ground-up development marks Hanover's Southern California industrial entry.
Industrial capital flowing to SoCal logistics/distribution despite higher construction costs.
stories.summary: Hanover Company and Crow Holdings Capital-advised fund broke ground on a 200,000-square-foot industrial facility on 13 acres at 903 Quimisa Drive in Simi Valley, California. The building features 36-foot clear heights, an 8.5-inch slab, skylights and ample parking, targeting corporate headquarters, packaging, assembly and distribution users. This marks Hanover's debut in the Southern California industrial market.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily. However, industrial expansion in Simi Valley signals logistics/distribution sector growth near major CA freeways; this can indirectly support local wage growth and worker population in-migration, supporting demand for nearby workforce housing in the Ventura County region over 2–3 years.

stories.title: Associated Bank Finalizes Loan for Twelve-Acre Retail Project in OH
stories.excerpt: Associated Bank announced the completion of a $9 million loan to GTZ Properties for development of Trailhead Crossing, a multi-building retail project at 1135-1131 US-36 in Delaware, Ohio, a suburb of Columbus. The twelve-acre project will consist of three freestanding buildings occupied by Chik-Fil-A, Chipotle Mexican Grill and Take 5 Oil Change; a second three-tenant strip will be occupied by Dunkin Donuts, Nothing Bundt Cakes and Pacific Dental Services. Of two pad-ready sites, one is already pending sale to a national daycare company. A later phase of the development will be anchored by a big-box national retailer. GTZ Properties is a Highland Park, Illinois, based full-service commercial real estate development and investment company specializing in retail-related properties nationwide that is headed by Mitch Goltz and Jeremy Forman. Daniel Barrins, a senior vice president with Associated Bank’s Commercial Real Estate division in Chicago, managed the loan arrangements and closing. This is Associated Bank’s 18th loan to GTZ Properties principal Mitch Goltz. The post Associated Bank Finalizes Loan for Twelve-Acre Retail Project in OH appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Associated Bank closed $9M construction loan for GTZ Properties' Trailhead Crossing retail project near Columbus, OH.
Multi-building retail project includes fast casual (Chipotle, Chick-Fil-A), services (Dunkin, oil change), plus pending daycare tenant.
Retail development capital available; modest local employment/population footprint unlikely to materially alter multifamily fundamentals.
stories.summary: Associated Bank finalized a $9 million construction loan to GTZ Properties for Trailhead Crossing, a multi-building retail development on 12 acres in Delaware, Ohio (Columbus suburb). The project includes three freestanding buildings housing Chick-Fil-A, Chipotle, and Take 5 Oil Change; a second strip with Dunkin Donuts, Nothing Bundt Cakes, and Pacific Dental Services; and a pending daycare pad-ready site. A later phase will be anchored by a national big-box retailer.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily. Retail development in Columbus suburbs does not signal material employment growth or population in-migration sufficient to drive apartment demand; these are consumer-facing service retailers serving existing residents, not anchor employers attracting new talent.

stories.title: Planet Fitness to Open at Sky Three Residences in West Brighton Beach
stories.excerpt: Planet Fitness has signed a lease for 14,520 square feet of retail space at the base of Tower 3 at Sky Three Residences, 532 Neptune Ave. in Brooklyn’s West Brighton Beach neighborhood. Located along the Neptune Avenue corridor, the new gym will complement the neighborhood’s growing mix of retail uses and is expected to open in early 2027. CBRE represented Planet Fitness in the transaction, while Commercial Acquisitions represented the landlord. Planet Fitness will join Sky Three’s growing ground-floor retail lineup, which includes CVS Pharmacy, NetCost Market, Starbucks, Flower Heaven NYC, Sky Mocha and Kings Barbershop. Flower Heaven offers Sky Three residents an exclusive 10% discount, while Sky Mocha provides delivery throughout the property’s amenity spaces, including directly to its resort-style pool. The post Planet Fitness to Open at Sky Three Residences in West Brighton Beach appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Planet Fitness leased 14,520 SF ground-floor retail at Sky Three Residences, Brooklyn West Brighton Beach.
Fitness anchor addition to residential mixed-use; opening early 2027 post-completion.
Retail amenity strengthens Sky Three resident retention and marketability but not demand signal.
stories.summary: Planet Fitness signed a lease for 14,520 square feet of ground-floor retail space at Tower 3 of Sky Three Residences (532 Neptune Ave., West Brighton Beach, Brooklyn), expected to open early 2027. The gym joins an expanding retail lineup including CVS Pharmacy, NetCost Market, Starbucks, and others. CBRE represented Planet Fitness; Commercial Acquisitions represented the landlord.
stories.impact: Not a demand or supply signal for development; this is an amenity lease at an existing/under-construction residential tower. Fitness + retail anchors enhance the project's appeal to residents but do not reflect broader market demand for new apartment supply in Brooklyn. No impact on future development decisions.

stories.title: Sheppard Takes 107K SF at In-Rel’s D.C. Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: One of the 50 highest-grossing law firms in the U.S. has signed an anchor lease at a planned Washington, D.C., trophy office redevelopment three years before its anticipated completion. Law firm Sheppard signed for 107,224 square feet at In-Rel Properties’ 2033 K Street NW, CBRE announced Tuesday. The firm, which has more than 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices, will move in after the building’s expected completion in July 2029. The brokerage did not disclose the value of the lease or the asking rent. In-Rel is expanding and updating the existing building, located along K Street near the intersection of D.C.’s Central Business District, West End and Dupont Circle. The developer will retain the property’s concrete structure while expanding it vertically and horizontally, including adding three floors and a penthouse. The renovations are another example of owners betting on Washington’s bifurcated office market, where distress coexists with a shortage of large, new trophy spaces, particularly for law firms and other high-end tenants. “We all know D.C. has plenty of office space, but what it doesn’t have is enough large-block, trophy-quality product that leading law firms like Sheppard demand,” In-Rel CEO Jackson Siegal said in a statement. Sheppard Chair Luca Salvi said the new office would provide a more modern and efficient workplace as the firm approaches its centennial and continues growing its Washington operation. CBRE’s Dimitri Hajimihalis, Emily Eppolito and Carroll Cavanagh represented In-Rel. Savills’ Gary Stein, David Lipson, Jon Glass and Owen Jaccard represented Sheppard. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Law firm Sheppard (top 50 U.S., 1,200+ attorneys, 16 offices) signed 107K SF anchor lease at In-Rel's D.C. office redevelopment.
Move-in date July 2029; building expands vertically/horizontally with three new floors and penthouse.
Major law firm commitment to new trophy office validates D.C. shortage of large, modern space; signals flight-to-quality.
stories.summary: Sheppard, one of the 50 highest-grossing law firms in the U.S. with 1,200+ attorneys across 16 offices, signed a 107,224-square-foot anchor lease at In-Rel Properties' planned redevelopment at 2033 K Street NW, Washington D.C. The firm will occupy the space after the building's completion in July 2029. In-Rel is expanding the existing structure with three additional floors and a penthouse while retaining the concrete core.
stories.impact: D.C. office market signal: major law firm pre-leasing three years before completion reflects acute shortage of modern, large trophy office space in the Central Business District. This confirms ongoing professional services job stability in Washington and validates capital deployment to Class A redevelopments. Does not directly signal multifamily demand but reinforces D.C. as a strong employment hub, supporting future residential demand for white-collar workers.

stories.title: Eliot Spitzer Gains State Approval to Redevelop 985 Fifth Avenue After Legal Bout
stories.excerpt: Former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer will finally get to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue after suing the state to obtain approval. Spitzer claimed that the state’s Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) was delaying the approval of an application to not renew rent-stabilized leases in the building, a necessary step before the property could be redeveloped. Spitzer ultimately won the state’s blessing. The two-year request to end the rent-stabilized leases on the property followed approval from the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 2023 to take a wrecking ball to the 25-story rental property and construct luxury condominiums in its place. Spitzer alleged potential misconduct in the lawsuit, reported by The Real Deal. Spitzer could not be reached for comment. HCR, now under the administration of Gov. Kathy Hochul, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Spitzer’s Spitzer Enterprises has been advancing on other aspects of the project despite the delay, unveiling designs by SLCE Architects for the property in November 2025 which would yield 25 condo units, according to New York YIMBY. The former governor, who resigned in 2008 during a prostitution scandal, has owned the property since at least 2018 after buying seven residential buildings in the city, including 800 Fifth Avenue, with a total of 1.5 million square feet. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Eliot Spitzer wins state approval to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan, after legal suit against HCR.
Rent-stabilized lease non-renewal cleared path to luxury condo redevelopment following LPC approval (2023).
High-barrier regulatory wins signal Manhattan condo development viability but limit rental housing stock.
stories.summary: Former New York Governor Eliot Spitzer obtained state approval to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue, a 25-story rent-stabilized rental property on Fifth Avenue, after suing New York's Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) to force approval of non-renewal of rent-stabilized leases. The New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission had approved the demolition in 2023. Spitzer Enterprises plans to replace it with luxury condominiums designed by SLCE Architects.
stories.impact: Negative for multifamily rental supply in Manhattan: removal of 25-story rent-stabilized building from market reduces available affordable/moderate rental stock on Fifth Avenue while shifting demand to remaining rental inventory. However, the two-year regulatory battle and legal action required to clear rent-stabilization leases signals high friction cost for Manhattan rental demolitions; this limits new multifamily development feasibility and makes ground-up apartment construction (vs. conversion or condo) less attractive in this submarket due to regulatory risk and timeline uncertainty.

stories.title: OCVibe Adds Five Dining Concepts to $5B SoCal District
stories.excerpt: The Samueli family has added five more dining concepts to the 50,000-square-foot market hall set to open next year as part of the $5 billion mixed-use development called OCVibe surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, Calif. Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll and Gelato Paradiso are the five new food options, adding Mexican, Filipino, Northern Chinese and Italian menus to the 21-kitchen market hall named Katella Commons. They join a growing roster at OCVibe, which earlier added concepts from chefs behind Amiga Amore, Burritos La Palma, Evil Cooks, Manaao Thai Comfort Food and Darkroom Restaurant and Wine Bar. Beloved Los Angeles chef Roy Choi is also bringing his Best Friend restaurant to the district. OCVibe did not disclose the values of the leases or the sizes of each space. Sources familiar with the development told Commercial Observer that OCVibe is fronting the initial investment, which averages around $300,000 per stall, as well as providing ongoing operational supports. “We wanted to approach this differently than a traditional landlord-tenant relationship,” OCVibe Senior Vice President Scott Frick said in a statement shared with CO. “Independent chefs are often asked to take on significant financial and operational risk before they ever serve their first meal. And unfortunately, many restaurants fail because of the significant upfront investment required of them.” Indeed, Frick recently told Commercial Observer that the Samueli family’s ownership structure has allowed the project to take a hands-on approach to restaurant leasing. Ownership is funding Katella Commons down to the kitchen equipment, allowing tenants to avoid substantial upfront costs of fitting out the new spaces. “Any tenant that comes in doesn’t have to come in with capital to fit out the kitchen — basically bring in your own knives and we’ll turn on the menu boards,” Frick said. bullets: OCVibe (Samueli family) adds five dining concepts to 50K SF Katella Commons at $5B Anaheim mixed-use district.
Food hall opening in 2026 includes 21-kitchen market with celebrity chef Roy Choi anchor.
Retail/mixed-use development around Honda Center signals Anaheim growth trajectory but not direct multifamily demand.
stories.summary: The Samueli family added five dining concepts—Don Churros Gomez, MFK (Modern Filipino Kitchen), Mojo, Pull & Roll, and Gelato Paradiso—to Katella Commons, a 50,000-square-foot market hall opening in 2026 as part of OCVibe, a $5 billion mixed-use development around the Honda Center in Anaheim, California. Roy Choi's Best Friend restaurant is also joining. OCVibe is fronting approximately $300,000 per stall in initial investment and operational support.
stories.impact: Mixed-use entertainment district growth around Honda Center (Anaheim) signals capital confidence in Orange County submarket but is primarily retail/hospitality focused. Indirect signal: major retail/entertainment investment anchoring a district can support surrounding multifamily if residential components are included in the master plan; however, the article does not indicate residential apartments as part of OCVibe, limiting the demand catalyst for nearby apartment development.

stories.title: The New School Sells Loeb Hall Residence to Hawkins Way Capital for $52M
stories.excerpt: In its third acquisition of student housing in Manhattan this summer, Hawkins Way Capital has purchased a residence hall near Union Square for $51.5 million from the New School, according to city records made public Tuesday. Hawkins, using the entity 135 E 12th Owner, bought Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, directly from The New School, records show. Joshua Bird, managing director and general counsel at Hawkins, signed the deal for the buyer, while Loretta Ferrari, chief financial officer at the New School, signed for the seller. “We’ve long been looking for the right opportunity in this neighborhood, and this property represents an ideal addition to our portfolio,” Ross Walker, managing partner at Hawkins, said in a statement to Commercial Observer. “Its location, existing student housing infrastructure and flexibility put us in an ideal position to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country’s strongest urban student housing markets.” It’s unclear why the New School stopped using Loeb Hall as an active dormitory for its students, but the property was removed from its undergraduate housing options this year. Loeb Hall is four blocks east of the New School’s main University Center and administrative offices on Fifth Avenue, although the sprawling urban campus has numerous sites near Union Square. The former Loeb Hall will undergo renovations and be repositioned under Hawkins’ Found Study student housing platform, according to a spokesperson for Hawkins. It’s unclear who brokered the recent sale. A spokesperson for the New School did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal is Hawkins’ third major student housing acquisition in Manhattan in recent months. bullets: Hawkins Way Capital acquired Loeb Hall student residence from New School for $51.5M (268 beds, Union Square).
Third Manhattan student housing acquisition by Hawkins in summer; marks institutional investor shift into student housing.
Institutional capital targeting student housing in Manhattan; asset sales by universities signal monetization of real estate.
stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital purchased Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street near Union Square, from The New School for $51.5 million. This marks Hawkins Way Capital's third student housing acquisition in Manhattan within the summer period. The property is adjacent to Union Square and provides existing student housing infrastructure.
stories.impact: Student housing market signal: institutional investor acquisition of university-owned residence halls indicates strong investor appetite and pricing discipline for stabilized, purpose-built student housing in Manhattan. While not traditional multifamily, this reflects capital redeployment away from value-add office and into housing assets. For multifamily developers, this signals that purpose-built student housing (near campuses, with 268+ beds) may offer better risk-adjusted returns than competing for general market-rate rentals in tight, competitive Manhattan submarkets.

stories.title: Fifth Third, CB&T TruAmerica Lend $124M on Bay Area Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: SummerHill Apartment Communities (SHAC) has landed $123.5 million of construction financing to build a multifamily project in the San Francisco Bay Area, Commercial Observer has learned. Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust (CB&T) provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan for the developer’s planned apartment community in San Carlos, Calif. TruAmerica Multifamily also closed a $27 million preferred equity investment to support the six-story San Mateo County development, which is slated to commence construction soon. The deal marked TruAmerica Multifamily’s first preferred equity financing since launching a structured finance platform last year. The new business vertical was formed following the addition of Ash Baraghoush, head of TruAmerica’s structured finance group, after he spent nearly a decade at Pacific Urban Investors. “This really goes hand in hand with the firm’s transformation into being a residential investment management company and being able to speak throughout the entire capital stack as opposed to just being owner operators,” Baraghoush told Commercial Observer. “We have spent a good year-plus cultivating new relationships.” Located at 11 El Camino Real 24 miles south of Downtown San Francisco, the project will feature 251 apartments with 38 of the units designated as affordable housing. Baraghoush said San Carlos has plenty of tailwinds as a multifamily market given its close ties to the San Francisco Bay Area’s technology and life science industries. He noted that the San Carlos submarket has a 97 percent multifamily occupancy rate and the region has experienced double-digit rent growth. “The Bay Area as a market has certainly outperformed and is perhaps one of the one of the better performing markets in the nation right now driven by return to office and driven by the AI boom,” Baraghoush said. “The need for affordable workforce housing continues to remain and that’s one of the attractive natures for this
bullets: Fifth Third Bank, California Bank & Trust closed $96.5M senior construction loan; TruAmerica provided $27M preferred equity for SummerHill multifamily project in San Carlos, CA.
Total $123.5M financing for six-story apartment community; TruAmerica's first preferred equity since launching structured finance platform.
Robust construction financing availability for Bay Area multifamily; capital stack diversification supports development feasibility.
stories.summary: SummerHill Apartment Communities (SHAC) secured $123.5 million in financing for a planned six-story multifamily project in San Carlos, California (San Mateo County). Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan, while TruAmerica Multifamily committed a $27 million preferred equity investment. Construction is slated to commence soon. This was TruAmerica Multifamily's first structured finance deal since launching a dedicated platform led by Ash Baraghoush.
stories.impact: Bay Area multifamily capital environment: robust construction financing availability and willingness of institutional equity/preferred partners to layer capital indicates lender confidence in San Carlos/San Mateo submarket fundamentals and rental demand. TruAmerica's new structured finance platform signals investor appetite for mezz/preferred equity in apartment development, broadening financing options and reducing cost of capital. This supports continued apartment starts in Silicon Valley suburbs facing housing supply shortages; favorable financing terms lower all-in development cost and make projects more underwritable in a higher-rate environment.
